quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 14

questions.question: A car is following you too closely on a two-lane road. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down slowly to let the car pass you.
Speed up to make more space between you.
Brake hard, then go back to your normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down slowly to let the car pass you.
questions.explanation: If a car is too close behind you, try to change lanes. If you cannot change lanes, slow down gradually. This lets the other driver pass you safely.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow truck.
To turn left into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn left into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing or lane changes. You can only cross them to turn left into a driveway or to make a U-turn where it is allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn.
No stopping.
No U-turn.
Detour ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn in this area.

questions.question: You come to an intersection blocked by traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move forward slowly as traffic moves.
Get as close as possible to the car ahead.
Wait outside the intersection until traffic clears.
Use your horn to make cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait outside the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if you cannot drive completely through it. Wait until traffic clears so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: You want to turn left at a green light, but traffic is coming from the other direction. What should you do?

options.text: Use the next intersection.
Wait at the edge of the road for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Turn immediately because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: When turning left with a green light, you can enter the intersection to prepare your turn. Wait in the center for oncoming traffic to pass before you complete your left turn.

questions.question: Dust or smoke is blowing across the road and blocking your view. You should drive slowly and turn on your:

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights when you cannot see other vehicles clearly. This helps other drivers see you too.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane, one-way street or highway, which lane should you start from?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, what should you do with your wheels?

options.text: Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill by a curb, turn your wheels sharply to the left, away from the curb. If your brakes fail, your car will roll into the curb instead of into traffic.

questions.question: What does a "No parking" sign allow you to do?

options.text: You cannot stop there at any time.
You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can park if you stay in the car.
You can leave your car for less than five minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No parking" sign allows you to stop temporarily to pick up or drop off passengers or goods.

questions.question: Why should you be careful when passing a bicycle?

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.
The cyclist may suddenly move into traffic to avoid something on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may suddenly move into traffic to avoid something on the road.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing bicycles. Cyclists may suddenly move into traffic to avoid objects on the road. Always drive cautiously around cyclists.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A railroad crossing is ahead. Be ready to stop.
You must always stop at the railroad crossing ahead.
Stop and wait for a signal before crossing the railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing is ahead. Be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a railroad crossing is near. Look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop. Wait for all trains to pass before you cross.

questions.question: You are driving defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Only look at the car directly in front of you.
Constantly scan the road to spot possible dangers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Constantly scan the road to spot possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means constantly scanning ahead for hazards. Do not stare only at the road right in front of your car. Watch the road far ahead and stay alert to vehicles around you.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road is getting wider.
The right lane is ending soon.
A highway entrance ramp is ahead.
The left lane is ending soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending soon.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the right lane will end soon. Be prepared to merge safely into another lane.

questions.question: A car is coming toward you with bright headlights. What should you do?

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other driver dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look away from the bright lights and toward the right side of the road. This prevents the lights from blinding you while the other car passes.

questions.question: Drivers should know that bicycles used after dark must have:

options.text: Reflective handlebar grips.
A front light and a red back light.
White reflectors on the front and back fenders.
Brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: A front light and a red back light.
questions.explanation: Bicycles used at night must have a front light visible from at least 500 feet away and a red back light visible from at least 300 feet away. These lights make the bicycle visible to other drivers in the dark.

questions.question: You are backing out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children you are moving.
Honk your horn so the children can hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Always get out and look behind your car before backing up. Do not rely only on mirrors, especially when children are nearby.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Right, not a privilege.
Privilege, not a right.
Requirement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege. You must earn it and follow the rules to keep it.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After turning, your car should be in:

options.text: The right lane.
The center of the street.
The left lane.
The lane with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: When you turn left onto a one-way street, end your turn in the left lane. This is the lane closest to where you came from.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing with no traffic signals. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will not happen.
Speed up to get across the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At an unmarked railroad crossing, slow down and be ready to stop. Look both ways on all tracks for trains. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance from the tracks. Wait until the train passes before crossing.

questions.question: You see or hear an emergency vehicle coming. What should you do?

options.text: Stop right away and let the vehicle pass.
Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
Drive slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle with lights and/or a siren, move as far right as safely possible and stop. Do not stop in an intersection.
